questions.stem: The one-dimensional Ising model with short-range interactions in zero field:

options.B: has no phase transition at any non-zero temperature

explanation.whyCorrect: Domain walls cost finite energy \(2J\) but gain entropy \(\sim k_B\ln N\); at any \(T>0\) long-range order is destroyed (Ising, 1925).
explanation.howToModify: Ask for the spin–spin correlation length in 1D (\(\xi\propto e^{2J/k_BT}\)).

questions.stem: The exact solution of the two-dimensional Ising model in zero field was obtained by:

explanation.whyCorrect: Onsager (1944) solved the 2D square-lattice model, finding \(k_BT_c = 2J/\ln(1+\sqrt2)\approx2.27J\).

questions.stem: The natural order parameter for the ferromagnetic–paramagnetic transition is:

explanation.whyCorrect: Magnetization is zero in the disordered phase and non-zero in the ordered phase, reflecting broken up–down symmetry.

whyWrong.B: A response function, not an order parameter.

explanation.trapUsed: Thermodynamic quantities non-zero in both phases.
explanation.howToModify: Ask for the order parameter of the liquid–gas transition (density difference).
explanation.howToAvoid: Order parameter: zero above \(T_c\), non-zero below.

questions.stem: A continuous (second-order) phase transition is characterized by:

options.A: continuous first derivatives of the free energy but singular second derivatives (e.g. heat capacity, susceptibility)
options.C: coexistence of two phases at the transition
options.D: latent heat and a jump in entropy

explanation.whyCorrect: At a continuous transition the order parameter grows continuously from zero; response functions diverge or jump.
explanation.howToModify: Ask for an example of each type (boiling vs ferromagnet at \(T_c\)).
explanation.howToAvoid: Second-order ⇒ no latent heat, singular response.

questions.stem: A 1D open chain of 4 Ising spins with \(H = -J\sum_{i=1}^{3}s_is_{i+1}\) (\(s_i=\pm1\)) is fully aligned. Its energy is:

explanation.whyCorrect: An open chain of 4 spins has 3 nearest-neighbour bonds, each contributing \(-J\).
explanation.howToModify: Ask for the energy with one spin flipped at an end (\(-J\)).

questions.stem: Near \(T_c\), magnetization vanishes as \(M\propto(T_c-T)^\beta\). Mean-field theory predicts \(\beta =\):

explanation.whyCorrect: Minimizing Landau's \(F = a(T-T_c)M^2 + bM^4\) gives \(M\propto(T_c-T)^{1/2}\). The exact 2D Ising value is 1/8; 3D Ising ≈ 0.326.
explanation.howToModify: Ask for the mean-field susceptibility exponent γ (1).
explanation.howToAvoid: Mean field: β = 1/2, γ = 1, δ = 3, α = 0 (jump).
